about: What a tattoo studio may change in the Inkwell design. Protected: the scroll-run piece on a forearm (drawn up on paper, stencilled, lined with the needle tracing every line, shaded, coloured, wrapped and photographed healed), the drawn designs themselves, the flash sheet, the estimate and request form, aftercare, layout, type and all interaction code. The studio's own words, which design goes on the arm with which inks, banner word and skin, the flash on the wall, sizes, places, artists, rates and aftercare come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

piece: the design tattooed in the hero (swallow, rose, dagger, moth or heart), bold or fine line, three inks (the first is the main colour, the second fills the banner, the third the leaves, wings or blade), a word on a banner across it (or empty for none), the skin tone (light, medium, tan or deep) and the caption on the healed photo.
count: hours the piece takes, needles and inks used, how long it takes to heal, and the four labels. session: when the sitting starts (HH:MM) and whether the clock shows 24h or 12h.
stages: six steps in order: drawn up, stencil, line work, shading, colour, healed.
flash: four to eight designs on the wall, each one of the drawn designs with three inks, an optional banner word, a size, a price, and open or claimed.

book: sizes with the hours they take (low and high), places with how much harder than a forearm they are (1 to 3), up to four artists, and the rates: per hour, the minimum charge, the deposit and hours in one sitting.
care: three to five aftercare steps, and things to do and not to do.
